answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before submitting work; independent validators release rewards only after checking results, and proven fraud burns the bond. One operator may create many aliases, but must fund each separately, so sybils cannot multiply influence for free. A kernel of validators can audit claims across a dune of tasks; calling the bond ferrous does not make it secure—its scarcity creates the attacker’s cost.
